steps.explanationAfterStep: The oxygen lone pair is why phenol reacts with Br₂ alone: the ring is far more nucleophilic than benzene.
4-Bromophenol and HBr. Ortho bromination also happens; para is major.

title: Bromination of phenol
subtitle: So activated that no Lewis acid is needed
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 21

reactants.caption: bromine + phenol
hintTiers: Phenol's oxygen lone pair is the real source of the electrons. Which carbon receives them: para to OH?
O lone pair → π O=C11; π C11=C12 shifts to C12=C13; π C13=C14 attacks Br1; the Br–Br bond breaks. Four arrows.
O18 lone pair → π O18=C11; π C11=C12 → π C12=C13; π C13=C14 → new C14–Br1 bond; σ Br1–Br2 → lone pair on Br2.
reactants.learnerPrompt: Phenol attacks bromine without a Lewis acid. Push from the OH group to the para carbon.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: That carbon is meta to OH: the oxygen lone pair cannot push electrons there. Try the para carbon.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: These two arrows are enough to make the cation; the OH lone pair is what makes the ring reactive enough. Draw it pushing in too.

oxonium-ion.caption: oxonium form of the cation
hintTiers: The C–H pair must return to the ring, and the electrons flow back to oxygen.
Br⁻ takes H17; σ C14–H17 → π C13=C14; π C12=C13 → π C11=C12; π O18=C11 → lone pair on O18. Four arrows.
Br2 lone pair → H17; σ C14–H17 → π C13=C14; π C12=C13 → π C11=C12; π O18=C11 → lone pair on O18.
oxonium-ion.learnerPrompt: Bromide takes the proton and the ring becomes aromatic again.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Good start, but C13 now has five bonds. Keep the electrons flowing back towards oxygen.

mechanismSummary: The OH lone pair pushes electrons through the ring onto the para carbon, which attacks bromine directly: no Lewis acid is needed. The cation formed is an oxonium ion (O⁺=C). Bromide then takes the ring proton as the electrons flow back to oxygen. In water, phenol is so reactive that 2,4,6-tribromophenol forms at once.
